MLM1 Logistics
This lecture covers MLM test material. 
At the end of this week you will have access to the MLM 1 
Attempt 1. 
Note: Once you open the at-home quiz you will have 15 minutes 
to complete the questions. Once that time is up, the quiz will 
close. This is to practice the same timing you will have in class 
next week in the In-class MLM1 (September 25).

Using your knowledge of properties of functional groups,  predict the types 
and relative strengths of non-covalent interactions that can form between 
biologically relevant functional groups within or between unfamiliar 
molecules.  To do this you will need to be able to:
Identify the types and relative strengths and chemical basis of 
noncovalent interactions between molecules or functional groups.
Recognize that highly electronegative atoms (for example O and N) lead 
to uneven electron sharing and permanent dipoles when bonded to other 
biologically relevant atoms.
Identify whether a molecule or group on a molecule is: polar or nonpolar; 
neutral or charged; hydrophobic, hydrophilic or amphipathic.
Learning Objectives

*You do not have to predict ions. Ions will always be notated with a plus or minus
High Electronegativity
Polar covalent bonds form between atoms with large differences in 
electronegativity. Look for O,N,S bonded with C,H,P. 
On the other hand, non-polar covalent bonds form between atoms with similar 
electronegativity. Common examples are C-C and C-H bonds.
